status_note: NOT frozen. This folder is not part of problems/ and gives no basis for a claim: WS1 has not frozen the problem, and selection/verify_claim.py does not know it. It only lets the research loop run on the problem (knockout --problem scout:third-autocorrelation-inequality).
title: Third Autocorrelation Inequality (Upper Bound)
solution_format: {"values": [f_0, ..., f_{n-1}]}: n finite floats, the values of f on n equal cells; negative values are allowed.

limits.notes: Loop-side limit, not a rule of the verifier: at most 131,072 values. The pinned verifier uses a direct O(n^2) convolution (0.2 s at 25,600 values, 1.2 s at 65,536, 4.7 s at 131,072). The sum of the values must not be close to zero.

verifier.source: EinsteinArena commit 5baf6361a3e0e2123edb98f676ef44f7ab081ad6; byte-identical to the live verifier at stage 2 (selection/registry_stage2.jsonl) and copied from selection/.cache/stage2/third-autocorrelation-inequality/verifier_pinned.py

independent.method: exact rational score by Kronecker substitution on big integers (no numpy, no floating point)

record_reference.rule: the exploratory gate compares with the lowest of: the live #1 (read from the API at run time), MILO's claimed value, and the score of the run's own warm start

live_top1_snapshot.label: verified: the pinned verifier reproduces it (docs/problem_scout.md)

milo_claim.source: https://jprithwish.github.io/MILO/ (demo data); arXiv:2609.38349 App. E.1 Table 13 prints 1.4488860143
milo_claim.label: claim: not on the leaderboard, construction not public, not reproduced by us

notes: [verified] The score is 2n * max_k (f*f)_k / (sum f)^2: scale-invariant, and the absolute value is outside the max.
[verified] Repeating every value k times (block repeat) keeps the score exactly; a finer grid only helps after re-optimization.
[verified] The live #1 (Atris, 65,536 values, score 1.449109789331911) has a third of its values negative.

[verified, scout] From the live #1: a 52 s cold polish of the log-sum-exp surrogate (T 1e-6 to 1e-9) gained nothing; a x2 block repeat with noise and a 75 s cooling ended 1.7e-6 worse; 12 re-melt hops (4 workers, 300 s) did not land once.

[verified, scout] In another basin on 25,600 values (near 1.44883), one re-melt hop (additive noise 1e-3 of the mean |f|, cooling 1e-3 to 1e-8 in 14 stages, 420 s) gained 2.7e-6, and a x2 block repeat with noise 1e-4 and a 420 s cooling gained 2.8e-6. Direct cooling paths that differ only by their first temperature (1e-3 to 1e-1) end up to 4.5e-5 apart, without a monotonic trend.

[claim] MILO (arXiv:2609.38349, App. E) reports 1.4488860143 on 25,600 values with: log-sum-exp surrogate, FFT gradient, L-BFGS stages on a geometric cooling ladder, a chain of re-melt hops with multiplicative jitter, 60 s runs. Its construction is not public.
[claim, forum] On erdos-min-overlap a sequential minimax LP polish (linearize the active lags, solve an LP, repeat) improved a smoothed-max solution at the end.
